subject: Linguistics
title: Reanalysis
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Reanalysis.

hook.text: 'A napron' became 'an apron'—speakers sliced the word boundary in the wrong place.

buildup.text: Reanalysis occurs when speakers assign a new structure to an existing form.

discovery.text: 'A nadder' became 'an adder,' and 'an ewt' became 'a newt'—the n jumped between words.

twist.text: Reanalysis can create new grammatical categories—'going to' was motion, now it marks future tense.

climax.text: This process is invisible to speakers—they don't realize they've restructured the form.

punchline.text: Cut a word in the wrong place and a new word is born.
